learning_objective: 🎯 Become a responsible digital citizen! Understand the ethical use of technology, the dangers of cybercrime, and the critical importance of managing e-waste.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every time you use the internet, you leave a trail. Active footprint is data you intentionally share (like a social media post). Passive footprint is data collected without you knowing (like your IP address or website tracking cookies).

Rights over creations of the mind. Copyright protects creative work (music, code). Trademark protects logos/brands. Patent protects inventions. Plagiarism is unethically copying someone else's work and presenting it as your own without credit.

Software where the source code is publicly available to view, modify, and distribute (like Linux or Python). It contrasts with proprietary software (like Microsoft Windows) where the code is hidden and owned by a company.

Illegal activities using computers. Cyberbullying is harassing someone online. Phishing is sending fake emails (like from a 'fake bank') to steal passwords. Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a system.

Electronic waste (old phones, batteries, broken computers) contains highly toxic chemicals like lead and mercury. Throwing them in normal trash poisons groundwater. They must be sent to authorized recycling centers.

fun_activity.title: 🕵️ The Digital Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Open Google and search for your exact name inside quotation marks (e.g., "Rahul Sharma"). Look at the images and links that appear. You are currently looking at your own public Digital Footprint!

exam_tips: 📌 Always clearly define Plagiarism: It is NOT just stealing; it is the act of stealing *and passing it off as your own original work*.
📌 Distinguish between Phishing (deceptive emails) and Hacking (breaking security protocols). Both are covered under the Indian IT Act (2000).
📌 For E-waste questions, always mention the environmental hazards (toxins leaching into soil) and the health hazards (neurological damage to sanitation workers).
quick_recap: ⭐ The internet never forgets; your digital footprint is permanent.
⭐ Open-Source software is usually free of cost, but 'Free Software' specifically refers to the freedom to study and modify the code.
⭐ Netiquette includes simple rules like not typing in ALL CAPS (which implies shouting) and respecting others' privacy online.
